subject: F0EB2ED42499EBA2278AA145E8D4C11A
introduction: John the Baptist matters to the Bahá’í writings in two ways. He is the type of the herald, and the Báb is constantly compared to him; and he is the test case for what “return” means, because the Gospels say both that he was Elijah and that he was not. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s explanation, repeated to many audiences, is that the qualities and mission returned, not the person: one lamp, another light. Nearly every reading rests on a verse, and the verses are set beside them here: the wilderness, the camel’s hair, “Art thou Elias? … I am not”, “Elias is come already”, “the spirit and power of Elias”, “he must increase”. The Qur’an adds its own annunciation of Yaḥyá. Plato on rebirth, and John’s question from prison, are the difficulties.
questions: John said he was not Elijah; Jesus said he was. How do the readings reconcile the two, and does Luke’s “in the spirit and power of Elias” support them?
What makes someone a herald? Why is it a hard station to hold?
Reading 7 says no dove came down. What principle of reading scripture is being applied?
“He must increase, but I must decrease.” Where in ordinary life is that asked of people?
John doubted from prison. What does that suggest about the followers of the Báb who did not accept Bahá’u’lláh?

outside.why: A physician of souls to a conquered people. O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance.
The reading retells this saying: John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, he hath a devil; the Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, behold a man gluttonous.
Cry out like John, make smooth the path. I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord.
Glad tidings to Zacharias of Yaḥyá. The Qur’an: Allah giveth thee glad tidings of a son whose name is John, who cometh to confirm a word from Allah.
O John! Hold fast the Scripture. And we gave him wisdom when a child.
He called the people to repentance before Christ. I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I.
Baptism was only a symbol of hearts purified. Jesus, coming to be baptized, to John who objected: suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness.

“The story about the dove is simply a metaphor. No dove came down.” The text: he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove. The Gospel itself says “like”. What does the reading’s insistence add, and what might a reader who loves the scene feel is taken away?
John felt that the Holy Spirit was in Christ. Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.
The reading cites this exchange: Art thou Elias? And he saith, I am not.
And this one: Elias is come already, and they knew him not. Then the disciples understood that he spake unto them of John the Baptist.
How both answers can be true. The angel had said it before his birth: he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias.
His soul was not the soul of Elias. The promise behind the question: behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord.

The readings use this case against reincarnation: the same qualities, not the same soul. Plato’s Socrates held the other view, that the soul has been born many times. How do the readings’ lamp and light answer him?
An explicit text of the Gospel. If ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.
His food was grass and honey. John had his raiment of camel’s hair, and his meat was locusts and wild honey.
The true herald, who makes ready the way. He must increase, but I must decrease.
The station of John. What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind? A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet.
His head severed for the sake of a harlot. The king sent an executioner, and he beheaded him in the prison, and brought his head in a charger.
The Báb a forerunner like John, like the dawn. He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light.

The Bayán’s people are to this Revelation as John’s followers to Christ. John himself, from prison, sent to ask: art thou he that should come, or do we look for another? If the herald could doubt, what do the readings expect of his followers?

malachi-i-will-send-you-elijah.text: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord

john-behold-the-lamb-of-god.text: The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world

matthew-reed-shaken-with-the-wind.text: And as they departed, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind? But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings' houses. But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet

quran-o-john-hold-fast-the-scripture.text: (And it was said unto his son): O John! Hold fast the Scripture. And we gave him wisdom when a child,

quran-glad-tidings-of-john.text: And the angels called to him as he stood praying in the sanctuary: Allah giveth thee glad tidings of (a son whose name is) John, (who cometh) to confirm a word from Allah lordly, chaste, a prophet of the righteous.
